newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: Colombian peso closes unchanged at 1,044.
newsitem.headline: Colombian peso closes unchanged at 1,044.

text.p: Colombia's peso closed unchanged at 1,044 as dollar buyers and sellers exerted equal pressure on the country's interbank market, dealers said.
They said the peso traded in a narrow 1,042.40 to 1,044.95 range and that upward or downward pressures on the local currency had basically negated themselves over the course of the trading day.

"The market was very even all day," one dealer said. "There were no fluctuations." He added, however, that state-run banks had jumped into the market to buy dollars several times during the session, in a possible bid to halt the peso's recent appreciation against the U.S. currency.
Further meetings of the committee have been scheduled for Wednesday but officials were unable to confirm whether or not they will take place.

A stronger peso makes Colombia's exports more expensive abroad, and the government and export sector have urged the central bank repeatedly to adopt measures aimed at undercutting the currency's recent rise.

Dealers reported 371 trades for a total of $132 million in Tuesday's session. There appeared to be little consensus on where the peso will be heading when banks move, as expected, to adopt new foreign exchange positions next month.
